items.tip: A telling sentence ends with a full stop.

no.?: This sentence tells us something. It doesn't ask, so it doesn't need a question mark.
no.,: A comma is a little pause in the middle. This sentence is finished, so it needs a full stop.
no.': An apostrophe goes inside short words like don't. It can't end a sentence.

items.tip: Do you…? asks something, so it ends with a question mark.

This sentence asks a question (Do you…?), so a full stop isn't enough.
no.,: A comma can't end a sentence. A question needs a question mark.
no.': An apostrophe goes inside short words like don't. It can't end a question.

items.tip: Every sentence starts with a capital letter: It is…

no.it: Every sentence starts with a capital letter, so we write It, not it.
no.IT: Only the first letter is a capital. IT in big letters looks like shouting!
no.It's: It's means it is. It's is a sunny day would say 'it is is'.

items.tip: Where…? asks a question, so put a question mark at the end.

Where is the jam? asks something, so it needs a question mark, not a full stop.
no.,: A comma is a pause in the middle. The question ends here, so use ?.
no.!: ! is for a big feeling or a shout. Where is the jam? is a question.

items.s: Bunny and ___ sit on the grass.
items.tip: When you talk about yourself, I is always a capital letter.

no.i: When I means me, it is always a big capital letter: I.
no.I'm: I'm means I am. Bunny and I am sit doesn't make sense.
no.i'm: i'm means I am, and it needs a capital I too. We just need I.

items.say: Bunny and I sit on the grass.
items.ask: Bunny and I sit on the grass.

items.tip: This sentence tells us what they eat, so it ends with a full stop.

no.?: Nobody is asking anything here, so no question mark.
no.,: The sentence is finished. A comma can't be the last mark.
no.': An apostrophe is for short words like can't, not for the end of a sentence.

items.tip: Can…? asks a question, so it ends with a question mark.

Can Bunny hop? asks something, so a full stop isn't right.
no.,: A comma can't end a sentence. This is a question.
no.': An apostrophe can't end a sentence. A question needs ?.

items.tip: A telling sentence ends with a full stop. If you feel very excited, ! is right too.

no.?: The picnic is fun tells us something. It doesn't ask.
no.,: A comma is a pause in the middle. The sentence ends here.
no.': An apostrophe goes inside short words. It can't end a sentence.

items.tip: What a…! shows a big feeling, so it ends with an exclamation mark.

What a beautiful unicorn! is a big 'wow' feeling, so it needs !, not a calm full stop.
no.?: It starts with What, but it isn't asking anything. What a…! shows a big feeling.
no.,: A comma can't end a sentence.

items.tip: Is it…? asks a question, so it ends with a question mark.

Is it your unicorn? asks something, so it needs a question mark.
no.!: ! is for a big feeling. This sentence asks a question.
no.,: A comma can't end a sentence. A question ends with ?.

items.tip: This sentence tells us a fact, so it ends with a full stop.

no.?: Her name is Sparkle tells us something. It doesn't ask.
no.,: The sentence is finished, so it needs a full stop, not a comma.
no.': An apostrophe goes inside short words like it's. It can't end a sentence.

items.s: Help___ The unicorn is stuck in the mud!
items.tip: Help! is a loud call, so it gets an exclamation mark.

no.?: Help! isn't a question. It's a loud call for help.
no.,: A comma can't join two sentences. Help! is a short shout of its own.
no.': An apostrophe goes inside short words. It can't end Help!

items.say: Help! The unicorn is stuck in the mud!
items.ask: Help The unicorn is stuck in the mud!

items.tip: How…? asks a question: How old is she?

How old is she? asks something, so a full stop isn't enough.
no.!: ! is for a big feeling. This sentence asks a question.
no.,: A comma can't end a sentence. Use ?.

items.tip: Ouch! shows a sudden feeling, so it gets an exclamation mark.

no.?: Ouch! isn't asking anything. It's a sudden 'that hurts' feeling.
no.,: A comma can't join two sentences. Ouch! is a little shout on its own.
no.': An apostrophe goes inside short words like don't. It can't end Ouch!

items.tip: A sentence starts with a capital letter: She lives…

no.she: Every sentence starts with a capital letter, so we write She.
no.SHE: Only the first letter is a capital. SHE in big letters looks like shouting!
no.She's: She's means she is. She is lives doesn't make sense.

items.say: She lives in a magic forest.
items.ask: She lives in a magic forest.

items.tip: How happy we are! shows a big feeling, so it ends with !.

no.?: It starts with How, but the words are in telling order (we are), so it isn't a question.
How happy we are! is a big happy feeling, so it needs !.
no.,: A comma can't end a sentence.

items.tip: Names of people start with a capital letter: Mia.

no.mia: Names of people always start with a capital letter: Mia.
no.MIA: Only the first letter of a name is a capital: Mia.
no.Mia's: Mia's means 'of Mia' (Mia's bag). Here we just need her name.

items.say: My best friend is called Mia.
items.ask: My best friend is called Mia.

items.tip: Days of the week start with a capital letter: Monday.

no.monday: Days of the week always start with a capital letter: Monday.
no.MONDAY: Only the first letter is a capital: Monday.
no.Monday's: Monday's means 'of Monday' (Monday's lesson). Here we just need the day.

items.tip: Names of places start with a capital letter: Singapore.

no.singapore: Names of places always start with a capital letter: Singapore.
no.Singapores: There is only one Singapore, so we don't add -s.
no.Singapore's: Singapore's means 'of Singapore'. Here we just need the place.

items.tip: A pet's name is a name, so it starts with a capital letter: Max.

no.max: Your dog's name is a name, so it starts with a capital letter: Max.
no.Max's: Max's means 'of Max' (Max's bone). Here we just need his name.
no.Maxs: There is one dog called Max, so we don't add -s.

items.s: On Friday, Mia and ___ play football.
items.tip: I (me) is always a capital letter, even in the middle of a sentence.

no.i: When I means me, it is always a capital letter, even in the middle.
no.I'm: I'm means I am. Mia and I am play doesn't make sense.
no.Im: Im isn't a word. We just need I.

items.say: On Friday, Mia and I play football.
items.ask: On Friday, Mia and I play football.

items.tip: The first word of a sentence starts with a capital letter: Our…

no.our: The first word of a sentence needs a capital letter: Our.
no.OUR: Only the first letter is a capital: Our.
no.Ours: We say Our teacher, not Ours teacher. Ours goes at the end: The teacher is ours.

items.s: Mr Tan has a cat called ___.
items.tip: The cat's name needs a capital letter: Tiger.

no.tiger: tiger with a small t is a big wild animal. The cat's name needs a capital: Tiger.
no.TIGER: Only the first letter of a name is a capital: Tiger.
no.Tigers: The cat is called Tiger. Tigers means lots of tigers!

items.say: Mr Tan has a cat called Tiger.
items.ask: Mr Tan has a cat called Tiger.

items.s: Next ___, we are going to the zoo.
items.tip: Days of the week start with a capital letter: Sunday.

no.sunday: Days of the week always start with a capital letter: Sunday.
no.Sundays: Next Sunday is one day, so no -s.
no.Sunday's: Sunday's means 'of Sunday'. Here we just need the day.

items.say: Next Sunday, we are going to the zoo.
items.ask: Next Sunday, we are going to the zoo.
